agentCan: Mint access tokens from the per-tenant ISU refresh token (refresh-token grant with Basic client auth) and call the tenant's REST/SOAP endpoints
Produce the customer-admin onboarding runbook (enable OAuth, create ISU/security group, register client, generate refresh token, secure hand-off)

approval.cost: No fee for registering an API client, and no Marketplace listing fee, is stated in the official public documentation read
approval.trigger: Vendor review of API clients: none. Workday does not review, approve, or certify tenant-registered API clients; registration is entirely an in-tenant administrative act. Who approves: the customer's own tenant administrator. The effective 'approval' is the customer tenant's security administration: enabling OAuth 2.0 Clients on the tenant, running the registration tasks, creating the ISU/security group, and granting domain security permissions. A third-party vendor cannot self-provision access to a customer tenant. No caps on API clients, refresh tokens, or connections are stated in the official documentation read. Listing is separate from API clients: a Workday Marketplace exists for distribution ('Workday Marketplace: Discover vetted solutions or learn how to list your own partner-built app'), and Workday's newsroom describes 'an expanded ecosystem of vetted, purpose-built solutions from Workday and partners, including those built with partner programs like Built on Workday, Workday Wellness, Global Payroll Connect, and Workday Agent Partner Network'. Listing runs through Workday partner programs rather than the tenant API-client mechanism; the public developer pages read do not document the review steps, eligibility criteria, or timelines for those programs.
approval.wait: None for API clients (no vendor review queue); Marketplace review duration not published in public official docs

blockers.detail: Registration returns a Client ID and Client Secret plus tenant-specific endpoints, and the refresh token is generated in the tenant UI by the customer's admin. Credential hand-off and per-tenant endpoint bookkeeping are part of the product design; there is no redirect-based 'Connect your Workday' flow the vendor can run once centrally.
blockers.howToClear: Ship a guided admin runbook and a secure credential intake; store tenant host, client credentials, and the ISU refresh token per customer.
blockers.title: No central connection UX

blockers.detail: The client's Scope (Functional Areas) caps what it may request, but actual data access is governed by the ISU's integration security group and domain security policies in that tenant. A correctly scoped client bound to an under-privileged ISU silently returns no data; a broadly-scoped client bound to a powerful ISU is a security exposure. Workday's docs recommend restricting assertion-grant clients to specific ISUs: 'If you don't select any ISUs in this field, the API client won't restrict access based on ISU user accounts... Workday recommends that you restrict the access of the client to specific ISUs.'
blockers.howToClear: Specify the exact functional areas AND the domain security permissions the ISU's group needs in the onboarding runbook.
blockers.title: Scopes are only half the permission story

blockers.detail: Per Workday's docs: 'Once you select this check box and click OK, you can't clear it.' The choice (bearer tokens with a 60-minute expiry that don't invalidate when sessions end) is permanent for that client.
blockers.howToClear: Decide the expiry posture with the customer admin before registration; a wrong choice means re-registering the client.
blockers.title: Enforce 60 Minute Access Token Expiry is a one-way door

alternatives: JWT Bearer Grant ('Use the JSON Web Token (JWT) for clients such as your Salesforce integration. This grant type enables you to restrict the exchange of security assertions for access and refresh tokens to Integration System Users (ISUs) you select'; requires an X.509 certificate for validating signatures)

SAML Bearer Grant ('Use for applications that use SAML SSO for authentication'; assertion verification via the configured IdP's X.509 certificate or a specified certificate; can optionally restrict to selected ISUs, or 'Allow Access to All System Users')
Interactive Register API Client (Authorization Code Grant, optionally with PKCE, with a Redirection URI) when a real end user must sign in and consent in a browser
ISU username/password WS-Security authentication for the SOAP Web Services (not OAuth)
Deprecated: Implicit Grant and the MAC access token type, both labeled '(Do Not Use)' with retirement planned in a future release
flavor.recommended: An API Client for Integrations registered in each customer's tenant, with a refresh token generated for a dedicated Integration System User (ISU)
flavor.why: The object is an API Client, registered inside a Workday tenant. There is no central Workday developer-portal app registration for API access; each client exists only within one customer's tenant. Workday's admin documentation covers two registration tasks: Register API Client (the general/interactive client, configured with a Client Grant Type and Access Token Type) and Register API Client for Integrations (the integrations variant, used with Integration System Users). Documented grant types: Authorization Code Grant ('Use for clients that can persist data, such as mobile applications'; PKCE support is an optional checkbox); Implicit Grant (labeled '(Do Not Use)'); JWT Bearer Grant; SAML Bearer Grant. Access Token Type options: Bearer ('Enables simpler development') and MAC ('(Do Not Use)'). For the recommended flavor the SaaS holds, per customer: tenant host/tenant name, Client ID, Client Secret, token endpoint, and the ISU's refresh token, and mints access tokens via the refresh-token grant.

humanMust: (Customer tenant security admin) Enable OAuth 2.0 for the tenant: in Edit Tenant Setup - Security, OAuth 2.0 Settings, select 'OAuth 2.0 Clients Enabled'

(Customer tenant admin) Create an Integration System User (ISU) and its integration security group; grant the group the domain security policy permissions for the functional areas needed; activate the pending security policy changes

(Customer tenant admin) Run Register API Client for Integrations (or Register API Client for interactive): Client Name, grant type, Access Token Type (Bearer), Scope (Functional Areas), optionally Include Workday Owned Scope, and refresh-token options

(Customer tenant admin) Record and hand over the issued Client ID, Client Secret, and tenant endpoints; generate the ISU refresh token (View API Clients > Manage Refresh Tokens for Integrations > Generate New Refresh Token)
name: Workday
nuances: PKCE is opt-in, not default: '(Optional) Select the Support Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) check box when using the Authorization Code Grant client grant type... Select this check box if the client will be supporting Cross Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)-enabled cross-origin requests.' Provider-stated time figure: the optional enforcement returns bearer tokens that 'Have a 60-minute expiry. Don't invalidate when sessions end, as long as they haven't expired'.

Certificate handling for assertion grants: JWT Bearer and SAML Bearer (with the x509 option) require an X.509 public key registered on the client (the certificate field 'is active when you select: Jwt Bearer Grant as the Client Grant Type' or SAML Bearer with certificate verification). 'Allow Integration Messages' can be selected 'to ensure that Workday receives necessary information about the status of the integration'.

The client's effective data access is the intersection of the client's scopes and the tenant's security configuration; endpoints (REST API, Token, Authorization) are tenant-specific and returned at registration.
prerequisites: A customer Workday tenant with OAuth 2.0 Clients enabled
A customer tenant administrator to perform every registration step
A dedicated ISU and integration security group per customer tenant

steps.detail: Prerequisite per Workday's docs: in the Edit Tenant Setup - Security task, in the OAuth 2.0 Settings section, select the 'OAuth 2.0 Clients Enabled' check box.
steps.title: (Customer admin) Enable OAuth 2.0 on the tenant

steps.detail: Create the ISU, place it in an integration security group, and grant that group the domain security policy permissions for the functional areas the integration needs; activate the pending security policy changes.
steps.title: (Customer admin) Create the ISU and security group

steps.detail: Run Register API Client for Integrations (recommended) or Register API Client (interactive): Client Name; Client Grant Type (Authorization Code Grant), Access Token Type (Bearer), Redirection URI (interactive clients), and Scope (Functional Areas); optionally Include Workday Owned Scope; set the refresh-token options; optionally select 'Enforce 60 Minute Access Token Expiry' (permanent once set).
steps.title: (Customer admin) Register the API client

steps.detail: Registration returns a Client ID and Client Secret plus the tenant's Workday REST API Endpoint, Token Endpoint, and Authorization Endpoint (tenant-specific). From View API Clients > API Clients for Integrations, use Manage Refresh Tokens for Integrations: select the ISU's Workday Account and choose Generate New Refresh Token. Hand all of these to the vendor securely.
steps.title: (Customer admin) Generate the ISU refresh token; hand over credentials

steps.detail: POST to the tenant token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token, the refresh token, and HTTP Basic client authentication (Client ID : Client Secret) to obtain bearer access tokens; call the tenant's REST API endpoint (and SOAP Web Services where applicable) with the access token.
steps.title: Mint access tokens; call the APIs

tagline: There is no Workday app to register: every connection is an API Client a customer's own tenant admin creates inside their tenant, bound to an Integration System User whose security group, not the client's scopes, decides what data you actually see.

time.active: ~1-2 hrs of customer-admin work + ~half a day of vendor integration code
time.total: Bounded by the customer's admin availability; no Workday queue
